What lets a bicycle roll? Choose from: wheel. leaf. egg.
Wheels turn and roll along the ground.
What cuts paper? Choose from: hammer. magnet. scissors.
Safety scissors cut paper. Cut away from your body.
What drives a nail into wood? Choose from: soap. hammer. screwdriver.
A hammer drives in nails. An adult helps with this.
What turns a screw? Choose from: screwdriver. hammer. fabric.
A screwdriver turns screws in or out.
What does a magnet attract: iron, wood or paper? Choose from: wood. paper. iron.
Magnets attract iron. Not every metal is magnetic.
What carries a path across a river? Choose from: lamp. bridge. wheel.
A bridge connects the two banks.
What lights up a dark corner? Choose from: lamp. wheel. sand.
A lamp gives off light when switched on.
What supplies energy to a battery-powered torch? Choose from: leaf. soap. battery.
A battery stores energy for the torch. Never open it.
What protects your head when cycling? Choose from: flower. helmet. paper.
A correctly fitted and fastened helmet protects your head.
What has teeth and passes on a turning movement? Choose from: gear. egg. glass.
Gear teeth fit together to pass on turning movements.
Which device tilts around a pivot? Choose from: battery. paper. lever.
A seesaw is a lever with a pivot.
What changes a rope's direction when lifting? Choose from: seed. pulley. soap.
A rope runs over a pulley, so you can pull down to lift something.
Which material can you see through clearly? Choose from: glass. wood. iron.
Clear glass lets lots of light through.
Which building material comes from trees? Choose from: water. water vapour. wood.
Wood comes from tree trunks and branches.
Which material makes a soft cloth? Choose from: iron. fabric. glass.
Fabric bends easily and can be made into a cloth.
What can you draw a building plan on? Choose from: paper. sand. oil.
You can draw a plan on paper before you build.
What helps you find north? Choose from: hammer. scissors. compass.
A compass needle lines up roughly towards north.
What can push a ball that is still? Choose from: moon. hand. cloud.
A hand can push the ball and make it move.
What does ice become as it warms and melts? Choose from: water. sand. wood.
Melting changes solid ice into liquid water.
What casts a clear shadow in lamp light: wood, clear glass or clear water? Choose from: glass. water. wood.
A wooden block blocks the light and casts a clear shadow.
What usually floats: a light dry piece of wood, an iron block or sand? Choose from: sand. wood. iron.
Many light woods float in water. A solid iron block sinks.
Which material lets light pass through clearly? Choose from: glass. iron. wood.
Clear glass is transparent. Iron blocks and wood blocks are not.
Which body part detects sound waves? Choose from: nose. eye. ear.
Your ears detect vibrations travelling through the air as sound.
What best softens tapping sounds on a table: a soft cloth, glass or iron? Choose from: iron. fabric. glass.
A soft cloth can damp vibrations and tapping sounds.
Which makes its own light: the sun, the moon or a cloud? Choose from: sun. moon. cloud.
The sun gives off its own light. The moon and clouds reflect light.
Which of these has its own solid shape? Choose from: oil. water. ice.
An ice cube is solid. Liquids such as water and oil take the shape of their container.
What forms invisibly when water evaporates? Choose from: wood. water vapour. iron.
Invisible water vapour forms. The white cloud in the game is only a symbol.
What supplies warmth that can melt ice outdoors? Choose from: sun. moon. rain.
The sun supplies energy. Ice melts when it warms enough.
What shows roads and paths in a drawing? Choose from: soap. salt. map.
A map shows paths from above on a smaller scale.
How do you hear a bicycle bell? Choose from: foot. ear. eye.
Your ears detect the sound of the bell.
Which material can make a strong wheel axle? Choose from: iron. water vapour. paper.
A metal axle can support and guide a wheel.
Which structure needs strong supports? Choose from: soap. egg. bridge.
A bridge needs a strong structure and suitable supports.
What soaks up water well when drying: fabric, glass or iron? Choose from: iron. fabric. glass.
An absorbent cloth holds water between its fibres.
What supplies energy to a solar cell? Choose from: sun. moon. egg.
A solar cell turns sunlight into electrical energy.
What turns on a moving bicycle? Choose from: scissors. salt. wheel.
The wheels turn as the bicycle moves forward.
What is a transparent window pane made of? Choose from: wood. glass. fabric.
Clear glass lets plenty of light into a room.
What can scissors cut: fabric, glass or stone? Choose from: fabric. glass. mountain.
Suitable scissors can cut fabric, but not glass or stone.
Which part of a pulley turns? Choose from: leaf. salt. wheel.
The pulley's round wheel turns as the rope moves.
What goes in a toy lamp's battery compartment? Choose from: wood. battery. ice.
Only the correct batteries go there. An adult helps replace them.
What has a north pole and a south pole? Choose from: magnet. roots. cloud.
A magnet has two poles. Matching poles repel each other.
Where can a fish breathe with gills? Choose from: water. sand. cloud.
Fish use gills to take oxygen from water.
Where does a blackbird hatch its eggs? Choose from: glass. oil. nest.
Blackbirds build nests for their eggs and chicks.
Where does a bee find nectar? Choose from: ice. flower. iron.
Many flowers contain nectar that bees collect.
What takes water from the soil into a tree? Choose from: roots. wheel. ear.
Roots take water from the soil.
What does a seed need to start growing? Choose from: oil. salt. water.
Many seeds need water, air and suitable warmth to germinate.
What gives a green plant light to grow? Choose from: iron. sun. moon.
Green plants use sunlight to make food.
Which animal develops from a caterpillar? Choose from: butterfly. frog. fish.
A caterpillar becomes a pupa. A butterfly emerges from it.
Which animal grows from a tadpole? Choose from: bird. cat. frog.
A frog tadpole develops into a frog with legs.
What can hatch from a hen's egg? Choose from: soap. bird. tree.
A chick can hatch from a fertilised hen's egg that is kept warm.
Which animal is a mammal? Choose from: cat. turtle. butterfly.
Mother cats feed their kittens with milk.
Which animal has feathers? Choose from: earthworm. fish. bird.
Birds have feathers, which help keep them warm.
Which animal has a hard shell? Choose from: mouse. turtle. bee.
A turtle has a shell that is part of its body.
Which animal loosens soil as it burrows? Choose from: earthworm. bird. cat.
Earthworms make tunnels in the soil.
What can grow into a new apple tree? Choose from: wheel. soap. seed.
An apple contains seeds that can grow into new trees.
Which animal can pollinate flowers? Choose from: turtle. bee. fish.
Bees carry pollen from one flower to another.
Which of these is part of a tree? Choose from: leaf. glass. wheel.
Many trees have leaves that absorb light.
Which is a fungus rather than a plant? Choose from: flower. bird. mushroom.
Fungi form their own group. Never eat an unknown mushroom.
What does a cat need to drink every day? Choose from: salt. water. oil.
Cats need fresh drinking water.
What might a blackbird eat? Choose from: earthworm. iron. glass.
Blackbirds eat earthworms and berries, among other foods.
Where can a butterfly drink nectar? Choose from: battery. hammer. flower.
Many butterflies use a long mouthpart to drink nectar from flowers.
Which of these animals lives in water? Choose from: bee. fish. cat.
The fish in the picture lives in water.
Where does a common frog lay its eggs? Choose from: water. desert. iron.
Common frogs lay their eggs in water.
What grows into the soil first when a seed sprouts? Choose from: flower. apple. roots.
A small root grows into the soil first.
What do roots absorb? Choose from: iron. water. paper.
Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals.
Where do many trees grow together? Choose from: forest. sea. desert.
Many trees grow together in a forest.
What changes colour on many trees in autumn? Choose from: iron. glass. leaf.
Many broadleaf trees have leaves that turn yellow, red or brown in autumn.
Which animal has a beak? Choose from: turtle. bird. cat.
Birds have beaks, often shaped to suit their food.
Which of these animals is an insect? Choose from: bee. fish. earthworm.
A bee is an insect. Insects have six legs.
What do young turtles hatch from? Choose from: apple. seed. egg.
Turtles lay eggs, and their young hatch from them.
What can form after flowering and grow into new plants? Choose from: soap. seed. iron.
Seeds can form after pollination.
What does a cat use to hear? Choose from: ear. wheel. leaf.
Cats hear with their ears.
Which is a living thing: a mouse, paper or glass? Choose from: flower. paper. mouse.
A mouse is alive: it grows, breathes and needs food.
What should you leave undisturbed when watching bird eggs? Choose from: soap. nest. wheel.
Watch a nest from a distance so the parents feel safe.
Which plant part holds a flower in the ground? Choose from: roots. wheel. bone.
Roots anchor the plant in the soil.
A plant's soil is dry. What might it need? Choose from: salt. oil. water.
The plant may need water. Give the amount that suits that plant.
What helps bees in a garden? Choose from: hammer. flower. glass.
A variety of flowers provides food for bees.
What can earthworms pull into the soil? Choose from: leaf. battery. glass.
Earthworms pull fallen, dead leaves into their burrows.
What do pond fish swim in? Choose from: paper. oil. water.
A pond contains water and is home to different animals.
What can grow from an acorn? Choose from: iron. tree. wheel.
An acorn is an oak seed. It can grow into a tree.
Which adult animal has four wings? Choose from: butterfly. cat. earthworm.
A butterfly has two forewings and two hindwings.
What does ice become when it melts? Choose from: water. sand. iron.
Ice is frozen water. Melting turns it into liquid water.
What can water become in a freezer? Choose from: salt. paper. ice.
When water gets cold enough, it can freeze into ice.
Which is liquid at room temperature? Choose from: glass. water. wood.
Water is liquid at normal room temperature.
Which is solid at room temperature? Choose from: wood. oil. water.
A block of wood has a fixed shape.
Which container reliably holds drinking water? Choose from: paper. fabric. glass.
An undamaged drinking glass does not let water pass through.
What dissolves in water: salt, sand or wood? Choose from: wood. salt. sand.
Small amounts of salt dissolve in water. The salt is still there.
What stays visible as grains in water? Choose from: sand. salt. water.
Sand does not normally dissolve in water.
What often forms two layers with water? Choose from: salt. paper. oil.
Cooking oil and water do not stay mixed.
What can help pick iron out of a mixture? Choose from: fabric. magnet. wood.
A magnet attracts iron. The metal picture here stands for iron.
What forms invisibly when water evaporates? Choose from: water vapour. wood. salt.
Water becomes invisible water vapour. The white cloud is only a symbol for it.
What are the little drops on a cold window made of? Choose from: sand. iron. water.
Water vapour in the air can turn into liquid water on cold glass.
Which form of water is solid? Choose from: paper. ice. water vapour.
Frozen water is called ice.
Which symbol stands for water as a gas? Choose from: water vapour. ice. wood.
Water as a gas is invisible. The vapour cloud is a simplified symbol.
What dissolves a little table salt well? Choose from: oil. fabric. water.
A little salt dissolves in water. Never taste an unknown substance.
Which material is transparent? Choose from: paper. glass. wood.
Clear glass lets light through so you can see through it.
Which material easily soaks up water? Choose from: paper. iron. glass.
Uncoated paper absorbs water between its fibres.
What can be softly folded up? Choose from: iron. glass. fabric.
A fabric cloth bends easily. A metal bar is much stiffer.
Which material can conduct heat well? Choose from: paper. iron. fabric.
Many metals conduct heat well. Never touch hot objects.
Which material often shows growth rings? Choose from: wood. glass. iron.
Wood comes from trees. Growth rings are often visible in a cut section.
What helps water wash away greasy dirt? Choose from: sand. oil. soap.
Soap helps water remove grease and dirt.
Which substance is often used in cooking and stays liquid? Choose from: salt. oil. ice.
Many cooking oils are liquid at room temperature.
Which of these consists of many little grains? Choose from: sand. glass. water.
Sand consists of many small solid grains.
What provides warmth that can melt ice outdoors? Choose from: moon. snow. sun.
The sun supplies energy. Heat can make ice melt.
Where do many tiny water drops gather in the sky? Choose from: wheel. cloud. bone.
Clouds contain tiny water droplets or ice crystals.
What are raindrops mainly made of? Choose from: water. oil. salt.
Raindrops are mainly liquid water.
What are snowflakes made of? Choose from: sand. iron. ice.
Snowflakes are made of ice crystals.
What takes the shape of a glass? Choose from: iron. water. paper.
Liquid water does not have its own fixed shape.
What keeps its own shape on a plate before warming up? Choose from: ice. water. oil.
An ice cube is solid and keeps its shape until it melts.
Which material can shatter if dropped? Choose from: fabric. paper. glass.
Glass can break. Let an adult clear away the pieces.
What belongs with water for safe handwashing? Choose from: battery. soap. hammer.
Soap is made for skin. Unknown cleaning products are not toys.
What is left when salt water completely evaporates? Choose from: salt. oil. wood.
The water evaporates. Dissolved salt can remain as crystals.
What can separate iron pieces from sand? Choose from: soap. cloud. magnet.
A magnet attracts the iron pieces, but normally not the sand.
Which substance flows from a tipped open bottle? Choose from: glass. water. wood.
Liquid water flows and needs a watertight container.
What is often made from plant fibres? Choose from: paper. ice. water.
Paper contains connected fibres, often from wood.
What is the same substance as water, but solid? Choose from: oil. paper. ice.
Ice and liquid water are the same substance in different states.
What is ordinary glass mainly made from? Choose from: egg. sand. flower.
Silica sand is an important ingredient in glass, made in very hot furnaces.
Which material can be made from woven threads? Choose from: fabric. glass. iron.
Many fabrics are woven from threads.
What rinses soap off your hands? Choose from: oil. salt. water.
Clean water rinses away soap and loosened dirt.
What stays solid in water at room temperature: glass, ice or salt? Choose from: salt. glass. ice.
A drinking glass does not dissolve in water during normal use.
An ice cube melts in a glass. What is there more of afterwards? Choose from: water. battery. oil.
Melting changes solid ice to liquid water. It does not make a new substance.
Which body part detects light and colours? Choose from: eye. ear. foot.
Eyes detect light and send signals to the brain.
Which body part detects sounds? Choose from: nose. hand. ear.
Ears detect sounds. The brain processes the signals.
What do people use to smell? Choose from: foot. nose. eye.
The nose contains cells that detect smells.
What helps you taste sweet and sour? Choose from: tongue. ear. bone.
The tongue has many taste buds.
What can feel whether a cloth is soft? Choose from: tooth. leaf. hand.
The skin on your hand contains touch receptors.
Which organ pumps blood around the body? Choose from: tooth. heart. stomach.
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood through blood vessels.
Which organs help you breathe? Choose from: lungs. brain. bone.
In the lungs, oxygen moves from the air into the blood.
Which organ processes information from your senses? Choose from: foot. tooth. brain.
The brain processes signals and controls many activities.
What forms the body's hard framework? Choose from: water. bone. soap.
The bones together form the skeleton.
What breaks food into smaller pieces in your mouth? Choose from: tooth. ear. foot.
Teeth break up food when you chew.
Where does food go after the food pipe? Choose from: eye. ear. stomach.
Food moves through the food pipe into the stomach.
What helps wash your hands clean? Choose from: sand. soap. oil.
Wash with water and soap, including between your fingers.
What is a good drink when you are thirsty? Choose from: water. salt. oil.
Clean drinking water quenches thirst without added sugar.
What do you often see outside when it is dark at bedtime? Choose from: lamp. gear. moon.
Night is dark. Sleep gives the body time to rest.
Which body part often wears a shoe? Choose from: nose. foot. ear.
Shoes protect feet. People move in different ways.
What protects your head when cycling? Choose from: helmet. soap. paper.
A well-fitted helmet can protect your head if you fall.
Which body part needs protection from very loud sounds? Choose from: tooth. stomach. ear.
Very loud sounds can harm hearing. Turn the volume down.
Which body part do eyelids protect? Choose from: tongue. eye. nose.
Eyelids protect the eyes. Blinking spreads tear fluid.
Which body part helps filter the air you breathe in? Choose from: nose. tooth. bone.
The nose filters, warms and moistens incoming air.
What do many children lose and replace as they grow? Choose from: bone. hand. tooth.
Baby teeth gradually make way for adult teeth.
Which body part usually has five fingers? Choose from: stomach. hand. eye.
A hand usually has five fingers. Bodies can look different.
What usually beats faster when you exercise? Choose from: heart. ear. foot.
The heart often beats faster to bring muscles more oxygen.
Where does air go when you breathe in? Choose from: tooth. bone. lungs.
Air travels through the airways into the lungs.
Where are many memories processed? Choose from: ear. brain. hand.
The brain helps you learn and remember.
What protects the brain as the skull? Choose from: bone. water. soap.
The skull bones surround and protect the brain.
Which organ mixes food and continues digestion? Choose from: ear. nose. stomach.
The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
What helps the tongue recognise flavours? Choose from: foot. nose. bone.
Smell and taste work together when you eat.
What do you use to wash your hands before eating? Choose from: soap. oil. salt.
Water and soap help remove dirt and many germs.
Which of these is food? Choose from: battery. soap. apple.
A washed apple is food. Batteries and soap are not.
What is inside a foot and gives it support? Choose from: water. bone. cloud.
A foot contains many bones that work together for support.
Where do signals from the ears go? Choose from: brain. stomach. tooth.
The signals go to the brain, which processes sounds.
Where do eyes send their signals? Choose from: foot. tooth. brain.
Eyes send signals to the brain, where images are processed.
Which organ brings oxygen from air into the blood? Choose from: ear. lungs. tooth.
Oxygen can enter the blood in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.
Which organ is a strong muscle in the chest? Choose from: heart. tooth. eye.
The heart is a muscle that works even while you sleep.
What usually feels soft and bendy? Choose from: glass. iron. fabric.
You can feel and fold a soft cloth with your hand.
Which body part do you clean with a toothbrush? Choose from: ear. tooth. nose.
Teeth need regular cleaning. An adult can help finish brushing.
What can you breathe through when resting? Choose from: nose. foot. hand.
When resting, air can enter through your nose.
What helps you hear this game's music? Choose from: tooth. stomach. ear.
The ears detect music. Keep it at a comfortable, quiet volume.
What does the body need to drink? Choose from: salt. water. oil.
Drinking water provides the body with fluid.
What can gently hold a soft ball? Choose from: hand. bone. tooth.
Hands and fingers can hold a ball. People also use helpful tools.
What shows Earth as a small sphere? Choose from: globe. wheel. egg.
A globe is a small model of Earth.
What shows places and paths from above? Choose from: paper. soap. map.
A map shows part of the world from above on a smaller scale.
What helps you find compass directions? Choose from: glass. compass. hammer.
A compass helps you find north and the other directions.
What rises high above the land around it? Choose from: mountain. river. sea.
A mountain is a high landform.
What flows in a channel through the landscape? Choose from: desert. forest. river.
A river carries water along its riverbed.
What is land surrounded by water on all sides? Choose from: cloud. island. mountain.
An island is surrounded by water on every side.
Where can you find a very large amount of salt water? Choose from: sea. forest. desert.
Seas contain salt water and cover large parts of Earth.
Where is there very little precipitation over a long time? Choose from: river. forest. desert.
Deserts get very little precipitation. Some deserts are cold.
Where do many trees grow together? Choose from: sand. forest. sea.
A forest has many trees and is home to many animals.
What can fall from clouds to the ground? Choose from: rain. wood. iron.
Rain falls from some clouds and brings water to the ground.
What falls from the sky as ice crystals? Choose from: sand. oil. snow.
Snow consists of ice crystals that fall from clouds.
What gives Earth light and warmth? Choose from: cloud. sun. moon.
The sun supplies Earth with light and warmth.
What orbits Earth? Choose from: moon. tree. fish.
The moon moves around Earth.
What connects two banks so a path can cross? Choose from: sand. cloud. bridge.
A bridge crosses an obstacle such as a river.
Where do many large rivers eventually flow? Choose from: forest. sea. mountain.
Many rivers flow into the sea. Others end in lakes or inland.
What can stay on some high mountains even in summer? Choose from: snow. oil. soap.
High up it is often colder, so snow can remain there.
What is often coloured blue on maps? Choose from: paper. iron. water.
On many maps, blue stands for water such as rivers and seas.
What does a forest symbol on a map show? Choose from: sand. forest. sea.
A forest symbol shows where a forest is. The key explains the symbols.
What does a bridge symbol on a map show? Choose from: bridge. egg. soap.
It shows a crossing over a river or another obstacle.
What covers more of Earth's surface: seas or land? Choose from: fabric. paper. sea.
Seas cover more than half of Earth's surface.
Where do raindrops form in the sky? Choose from: wood. cloud. iron.
Tiny drops in clouds can join together and fall as rain.
What supplies energy for evaporation in the water cycle? Choose from: sun. moon. paper.
Warmth from the sun helps water evaporate.
How can water return from clouds to the ground? Choose from: sand. wood. rain.
Precipitation such as rain returns water to the ground.
Where can a river begin high above the plains? Choose from: fabric. mountain. sea.
Many rivers begin in mountains, but not all do.
What lies in little grains on many beaches? Choose from: sand. soap. iron.
Many beaches have sand. Others have pebbles or rocks.
What is especially scarce in dry deserts? Choose from: oil. salt. water.
Water is scarce in dry deserts. Living things there are adapted to this.
What surrounds an island in the sea? Choose from: mountain. sea. forest.
A sea island has seawater on every side.
What belongs in a forest? Choose from: tree. fish. glass.
Trees are an important part of a forest.
What can be folded up and show your walking route? Choose from: globe. ice. map.
A paper map folds up and can be used on a walk.
Which model shows Earth's other side when you turn it? Choose from: wheel. globe. bridge.
Turning a globe lets you see other parts of Earth.
What can hide the sun in the sky? Choose from: cloud. bone. iron.
Clouds can partly or completely block sunlight.
What can help melt snow in spring? Choose from: moon. paper. sun.
Snow can melt when the sun warms the ground.
What is long, flows and has two banks? Choose from: island. river. sea.
A river flows between its two banks.
Which landscape has a high peak? Choose from: mountain. forest. sea.
A mountain has a summit. Not every summit is pointed.
Which large body of water is normally salty? Choose from: river. paper. sea.
Seawater contains dissolved salts. Do not drink it.
What helps you line a map up with north? Choose from: salt. compass. soap.
A compass helps you align the map's north direction.
Which kind of precipitation is liquid? Choose from: rain. snow. sand.
Rain falls as liquid drops. Snow falls as solid ice crystals.
Which is a star: the sun, a cloud or the moon? Choose from: cloud. moon. sun.
The sun is a star and gives off its own light.
Where does the light reflected by the moon come from? Choose from: paper. sun. forest.
The moon does not make its own light. It reflects sunlight.
What do rain and rivers bring to many plants? Choose from: water. oil. salt.
Rain and rivers can supply plants with water.
